stimulus.text:
United States military occupations in Latin America came to an end in the 1930s.

| Country | Year the last United States Marines left |
| Nicaragua | 1933 |
| Haiti | 1934 |

Paraphrase: At the Inter-American Conference in Montevideo, Uruguay, in December 1933, Secretary of State Cordell Hull signed a declaration that no nation has the right to interfere in the internal or external affairs of another nation.
stimulus.source_note: Occupation end years from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.11, and Princeton Review, Chapter 11. Montevideo declaration paraphrased from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.11.

source: original; table from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.11, and Princeton Review, Chapter 11; Montevideo declaration paraphrased from Barron's
stem: Princeton Review notes that the Good Neighbor Policy was partly misleading, because the United States kept pursuing its interests in Latin America through economic pressure and support for pro-American leaders. That point best supports which conclusion?

options.text: The Good Neighbor Policy changed nothing at all
options.misconception: Occupations ended and the Platt Amendment was repealed; that was real change.

options.text: The methods changed more than the goals did
Latin America became fully independent of the United States
options.misconception: Economic pressure and supported leaders kept American influence strong.

options.text: The United States abandoned all interest in the hemisphere
options.misconception: Trade agreements and base arrangements show continued interest.

rationales.A: Background from the books: ending the occupations and repealing the Platt Amendment were real changes.
rationales.B: Troops left, but trade pressure and backing for friendly leaders kept American influence in place.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Princeton Review says the United States kept promoting its interests, often to the harm of local people.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934 deepened trade ties instead of cutting them.
rationales.general:
1. The table shows the military side of the Good Neighbor Policy: the occupations ended.
2. Princeton Review adds that the United States still pursued its interests, by economic pressure and by backing pro-American leaders.
3. So the troops went home while the influence stayed, in a different form.
4. That is change in method with continuity in goals, not a full break or no change at all.
Remember: ask what stayed the same when a policy claims to change.
